newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel loses three soldiers, wants Lebanon deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel loses three soldiers, wants Lebanon deal.

text.p: Israel said on Friday that it had no territorial designs on Lebanon and wanted to talk peace, a day after Hizbollah guerrillas killed three of its soldiers in fierce clashes in south Lebanon.
Despite the peace overture, Israel twice sent its warplanes to attack suspected guerrilla targets in south Lebanon, Lebanese security sources said.

"Israel has already clarified several times that it has no territorial interest in Lebanon. We are interested in reaching a real agreement in Lebanon," Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh said after the government's weekly meeting.

Naveh said Israel had "only one goal and that is the protection of our citizens ... on the northern border and we certainly are willing to enter discussions with the government of Lebanon, I think in this connection also with the government in Damascus, in order to reach an agreement that will ensure the security of the northern communities."
Israel's northern army commander, Amiram Levine, in a news conference broadcast on Israel Radio, said during Thursday's fighting there was an exchange of fire between Israeli and Lebanese forces.

"Terrorists both from the villages and Lebanon army forces tried to obstruct the evacuation operation ... and the rescue forces were forced obviously to fire at anyone who obstructed the evacuation, including at the Lebanese Army.
"Usually the Lebanese Army is not our enemy ... but anyone who participates in battle with Hizbollah and obstructs Israeli army operations and endangers it will be hit," Levine said.

In Beirut, a Lebanese Army spokesman said that during Thursday night's clash an Israeli helicopter fired a rocket at a Lebanese army position, destroying one armoured vehicle but causing no casualties.

On Friday, Lebanese security sources said two Israeli planes fired several rockets in each of the raids on ad-Dahr Daidaba ridges south of Syrian-controlled Bekaa valley. There was no immediate word on casualties.
The raids targeted the area where pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas clashed with the Israeli forces, killing three soldiers and wounding seven, according to Israeli army.
Security sources had said Israeli helicopters twice struck Hizbollah bases just outside the zone after the clash overnight.
The deaths brought to nine the number of Israeli soldiers killed and to 35 the number wounded in guerrilla attacks in south Lebanon this year. Last year 27 Israeli soldiers were killed in Lebanon.
Lebanon has followed Syria's lead in peace moves with Israel that began in 1991. But peace talks between Israel and Syria broke down in early 1996.

Hizbollah (Party of God) is fighting to oust some 1,000 Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong allied South Lebanon Army militia holding the south Lebanon zone set up by Israel in 1985 to protect its northern border area from guerrilla raids.
In Beirut, Hizbollah leader Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah said on Friday: "If Jews do not return to where they came from, the Islamic guerrillas' fists will throw all invaders and occupiers in the sea."
